analyzed_vuln.description: After the initial `GROW` of an external parsed entity, this function fails to honor a fatal parser halt. `xmlParserGrow` can call `xmlHaltParser` on an input-buffer growth/allocation error, which sets `instate` to `XML_PARSER_EOF`, frees the input buffer, and replaces `base/cur/end` with the global empty-string sentinel. `xmlParseExternalEntityPrivate` then unconditionally assigns `ctxt->instate = XML_PARSER_CONTENT` at line 12897 and calls `xmlParseContent`, reviving the halted context with invalid/sentinel input state. The subsequent `RAW` access in `xmlParseContentInternal` at parser.c:9957 produces the reported global-buffer-overflow. The fix belongs in `xmlParseExternalEntityPrivate`: return/clean up if `GROW` or encoding setup halted the parser, rather than overwriting EOF.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The schema fuzz input's first four bytes set `maxAlloc` to zero, so allocations are denied during parsing after the fuzz entities were registered. The main XML declares and references an external general parsed entity (`a`); the fuzz entity loader supplies its short crafted contents. Parsing `&a;` reaches `xmlParseReference` and `xmlParseExternalEntityPrivate`. Initial growth/encoding handling of that external entity encounters the forced resource failure and halts the entity parser. The vulnerable unconditional state reset then resumes content parsing on the halted input and triggers the out-of-bounds global read.

args: Inspect libxml2/parser.c function xmlParseExternalEntityPrivate and identify the safest cleanup/control-flow fix when its initial GROW or encoding setup changes ctxt->instate to XML_PARSER_EOF. Compare nearby parser entry points for established patterns that check fatal halt after GROW or xmlSwitchEncoding. Explain which return value and cleanup path should be used.

The reported ASan crash occurs because xmlParserGrow during the initial GROW can invoke xmlHaltParser after allocation failure, freeing the input buffer and setting base/cur/end to a global empty sentinel while setting instate XML_PARSER_EOF. xmlParseExternalEntityPrivate later unconditionally sets instate XML_PARSER_CONTENT and invokes xmlParseContent, causing RAW to read before/around the sentinel. The provided schema harness PoC forces maxAlloc to zero and reaches this path through an external general parsed entity. We need edit only libxml2 source and preserve all function-owned cleanup, so I am determining whether to jump to an existing cleanup label or return after freeing the temporary parser context.
